purpose: Resolve the four remaining even tangencies of the split Clifford branch curve, prove exactly one binary normalized-sheet pairing at each resolved node, enumerate all 16 raw pairing patterns, and quotient by the full component-sheet relabeling action with coverage and disjointness certified.

definitions.bit_semantics: 0 and 1 are the two equivariant bijections between the two unramified normalized cover fibers after resolving the corresponding even tangency; changing local sheet labels changes the bit by XOR.

local_pairing_lemma.statement: After the displayed blowup each even tangency becomes one transverse node, and each incident normalized ruling cover is unramified with a two-point fiber. An admissible deck-equivariant gluing is therefore a bijection between two two-point torsors; there are exactly two such bijections, identity and crossed.

sheet_relabeling_action.relation: delta_C0 XOR delta_Cr XOR delta_Cq = 0000 on pairing bits
sheet_relabeling_action.explanation: Flipping a component sheet label toggles every pairing bit at even-contact nodes incident to that component. The simultaneous deck flip on all three normalized components changes no pairing bit, so the effective relabeling group has rank 2.

orbit_invariants.interpretation: The two independent cycle parities in the unramified even-contact gluing graph.

exact_conclusion: The four-contact local/global gluing search is finite and completely reduced: 16 raw binary pairing patterns form exactly four isomorphism orbits under component sheet relabeling, classified by the two parity bits (L,R). No additional local sheet-glue choices exist at the four even contacts. The named CV J2 orbit is not selected in this certificate.
semantic_limit: The four pairing orbits are a common finite standard form for the next named-CV comparison, but no identification with the fixed marked Brauer basis [beta1,beta2], no equality with the named CV J2 class, and no torsor/lattice fingerprint is inferred from the cardinality four or the two-bit notation.
